text:
nina.sales: POC blocked for ShopWave. Okta group push shows 204 but no users created in shopwave-poc. Their SAML NameID is 'transient' and the Okta admin says their outbound proxy adds an auth header. cc @jasper.eng @mina.se
jasper.eng: 204 from Okta only means our endpoint returned 2xx. Can you ask for the raw request headers from their Okta logs? If a proxy rewrites or injects Authorization we may reject the request or see wrong token.
okta-admin: attached Okta audit screenshot. It says SCIM POST -> /scim/v2/Users returned 204. The outbound proxy at the customer adds header X-Forwarded-For and sometimes rewrites Authorization.
mina.se: that matches a pattern we've seen. If the proxy strips the original Bearer token or replaces Authorization, our SCIM endpoint returns 401/403 but Okta still marks the push as successful. Two fixes: 1) have the proxy pass through Authorization untouched; 2) use mTLS or a static IP allowlist if they can't avoid rewriting. Also NameID transient is not usable for login mappingwe need email in NameID or an email attribute.
nina.sales: they asked if we can temporarily issue a scoped hosted key so they can run a Dedicated throughput smoke test while they fix the proxy and mapping. They want to run a 30min run on pool 'dedicated-smoke-b'.
kevin.ops: we can create a scoped short-lived key: tmp_shopwave_30m, scopes=["inference:generate"], pool=dedicated-smoke-b, expires_in=1800s. But note: hosted API keys != SCIM tokens. SCIM requires the scim service token bound to /scim endpoints. Don't mix them.
okta-admin: they confirm they mistakenly copied the onboarding API key into Okta's SCIM Bearer field.
mina.se: that's the problem. Okta will happily send it and our endpoint will reject if it's not the correct SCIM token. Action items: - we will issue a scim token scim_shopwave_24h and a temporary infer key tmp_shopwave_30m. - customer to update Okta SCIM Bearer to scim_shopwave_24h and change NameID to EmailAddress or map user.email into SAML. - if proxy rewrites Authorization, recommend using mTLS or adding a small proxy rule to exclude the SCIM target from header modification.
sec-bot: Note: For Private/VPC POCs we prefer mTLS; for hosted trials bearer tokens are acceptable but must be DM'd to the designated admin. Never paste secrets in ticket screenshots.
kevin.ops: created tokens: scim_shopwave_24h (expires=1795088868), tmp_shopwave_30m (expires=1795004768, scopes=[inference:generate], pool=dedicated-smoke-b). I'll DM the secrets to the POC contact. Annotated: rotate on expiry.
okta-admin: thanks. We'll swap the Bearer token and re-run a manual group push. If it still shows 204 but no users, what should we ask them to capture?\asper.eng: ask them to capture the raw HTTP request/response pair from their proxy (headers+body) on the moment of push and paste in a secure upload. Specifically: Authorization header, Content-Type, Host, and any X-Forwarded-* headers. Also include our SCIM response body if present. Run this curl from their network to validate auth:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer SCIM_SHOPWAVE_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" https://scim.redwood-inference.example.com/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig
```
nina.sales: forwarding tokens now via DM. telling them to change mapping to user.login for externalId and set NameID to email. i'll update thread once they re-run group push. thanks all. :pray:
